message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **long weekends** that Canadians could enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a statutory holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day (observed Mon Jan 2) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Alberta, BC, NB, ON, PEI, SK, MB) | Family Day was on Monday Feb 20. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Good Friday was on Friday Apr 7. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day was on Monday May 22. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (observed Mon Jul 3) | Canada Day fell on Saturday, so the holiday was observed on Monday. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | Labour Day was on Monday Sep 4. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving was on Monday Oct 9. |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day (observed Mon Nov 13) | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, so the holiday was observed on Monday. |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day was on Monday Dec 25. |

> **Quick note:**  
> - Some provinces have additional holidays that can create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in Prince Edward Island, etc.).  
> - Boxing Day (Dec 26) is a statutory holiday but it falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does not create a long weekend unless you take a day off.  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
